assembly_notes:
Frame: +Z is up, the worm turns about +Z with its button on top, and the string post turns about +Y and projects toward +Y. The decorated cover/screw face is -Y, which is both the majority of the source pool (002, 004, 005) and the octant the shared preview camera looks from. Units repeat along +X.

Unit i is placed at x_i = i * unit_pitch_m. The driven wheel centre IS the unit origin, and the worm axis runs through (x_i - center_distance_m, 0, 0). Both rotors are authored centred on their own joint origin so mate_axes / register_interface_mate see a real axis, and so the worm screw and the wheel share the z = 0 mesh plane.

The mesh is the load-bearing derivation. SpurGear.r0 = module * teeth / 2 and Worm.r0 = module / (2 tan lead) in sdk/v0/gears.py, so tangent pitch circles mean exactly center_distance_m = gear_pitch_r_m + worm_pitch_r_m. Everything else -- the worm boss station, the mount's left edge, the gear chamber, the strip length -- is measured from it. Tooth tips interpenetrate by a fraction of a millimetre at a volume far below the SDK threshold, so no allow_overlap is used or needed.

Host adaptation across slots is by derivation, never exclusion. gear_chamber_r_m and mount_body_r_m are cut and grown from whichever wheel the active post presents, so a 30-tooth high_ratio_post fits inside sealed_housing, die_cast_housing and gearbox_bulb as well as it fits the open plates -- this mirrors the source fork, whose plate grew from 28x32 to 34x42 mm when its wheel went from 14 to 21 teeth. unit_pitch_m takes the widest of the wheel, button and centre-distance envelopes, so a large cloverleaf spreads the strip instead of colliding with its neighbour. button_seat_z_m is measured from mount_top_z_m, so a tall eared plate and a short die-cast block both get a button that clears them by the 3 mm 005 asserts.

Fits are real, not interpenetrations: every bore is shaft + 0.4 mm, inside the 1 mm gap the baseline QC still counts as support, and the worm and wheel are held at the pitch line by the centre distance rather than pushed into each other.

locking_split_post is the one candidate that changes the part and joint count: it adds a lock_screw part per unit on its own continuous joint about the post axis, which is what its source does. That is carried in a second category anchor rather than hidden.

derived.name: center_distance_m
derived.rationale: The mount places its worm bearings exactly one centre distance to -X of the wheel it is fitted with, so the pitch circles stay tangent for every tooth count and every lead angle. This is the binding that makes the mesh correct rather than approximately correct.

derived.name: gear_chamber_r_m
derived.rationale: The clear space the mount hollows out around whichever wheel arrives. This is the host adaptation that lets a 30-tooth high_ratio_post live inside sealed_housing, die_cast_housing or gearbox_bulb instead of the combination being excluded.

derived.name: mount_body_r_m
derived.rationale: The mount's outer envelope at the wheel station grows with the wheel: the gear lobe of an open plate, the bulb of a pod, the block half-height of a die casting. Mirrors the source fork, whose plate went 28x32 to 34x42 mm when the wheel went 14 to 21 teeth.

derived.name: post_bore_r_m
derived.rationale: The journal is bored to the shank the active post candidate presents, on a running clearance under the 1 mm support gap.

derived.name: worm_ratio
derived.rationale: The mimic multiplier the mount's post joint carries is -1/gear_teeth, so swapping the post candidate really does change the reduction.

derived.name: button_seat_z_m
derived.rationale: The button sits 3 mm above whatever height the active mount's upper worm bearing reaches, so a tall eared plate and a short die-cast block both get a button that clears them.

derived.name: unit_pitch_m
derived.rationale: The strip's unit spacing is driven by whichever of the three rotating or fixed envelopes is widest. The button term normally wins, so fitting a large cloverleaf really does spread the tuners along the mount.

derived.name: worm_shaft_r_m
derived.rationale: The shaft, its bearing bore and the button's hub bore are all one fit derived from the worm the lead angle produced.

derived.name: post_exit_y_m
derived.rationale: Where the +Y face of the journal actually is, given the wheel face width the active post presents and the wall of the active mount. A thin bracket and a thick die casting put it in different places.

derived.name: post_free_len_m
derived.rationale: The post's modelled shank is post_reach_m beyond post_exit_y_m plus the journal depth behind it, so the visible projection is honest and the post is always carried by the bore rather than cantilevered off the wheel.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: 1 <= tuner_count <= 3. The loop is index-general -- every station is re-derived from unit_pitch_m and nothing is indexed by a literal -- so the ceiling is budget, not mechanism. At N=3 with locking_split_post the seed builds 10 parts and 9 joints, each carrying tessellated involute worm and wheel solids; the pool's own maximum is also 3 (three_on_strip). A real six-a-side headstock strip is therefore not reproduced at full count, as recorded in the SourceMap's N derivation.
multiplicities.name: tuner_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: unit i sits at x_i = i * unit_pitch_m along +X, with unit_pitch_m derived from the widest of the wheel, button and centre-distance envelopes. Each unit contributes one worm rotor part, one string post part (plus one lock screw under locking_split_post) and its own mimic pair, and the mount grows from mount_x0_m to (N-1)*unit_pitch_m + mount_body_r_m. This is exactly the rule three_on_strip L308/L323 applies at N=3 (`WORM_CENTER[0] + x_m`), and staggered_posts L338/L348 applies at N=2.

candidates.evidence: _mounting_plate_shape is a filleted stamped rectangle unioned with a large gear lobe and a small lower lobe, then pierced for the post journal and two screws. The worm runs in two free-standing _annular_bearing_shape rings on bridge tabs, so the gear train is fully exposed.

dimensions.extent: a disc of radius mount_body_r_m about the wheel station

candidates.name: open_plate
candidates.notes: One welded stamped plate standing in the XZ plane: a filleted rectangle unioned with a gear lobe of radius mount_body_r_m at each wheel station and a smaller lower lobe at each worm station, pierced by the post journal and two screw clearances. The worm runs in two free-standing annular bearing rings carried on bridge tabs, so the whole train stays visible -- 001 L26-L73. Joint: root part; parents every worm rotor (continuous, +Z) and every string post (continuous, +Y).

parameters.name: gear_module_m
parameters.rationale: Tooth module shared by the worm and the driven wheel -- the one number that sets both pitch radii and therefore the centre distance. Pool: 0.00062 and 0.00066 (005 L177/L245/L307), 0.0008 (003 L134/L158), 0.0010 (001 L298/L354), 0.0012 (002 L230/L281, 004 L283).

parameters.name: worm_lead_angle_rad
parameters.rationale: Lead angle of the one-start worm. Worm.r0 = module / (2 tan lead) in sdk/v0/gears.py, so this is a real geometric parameter: it changes the worm's own diameter and hence the centre distance and the mount's worm boss. Pool: 8 deg (002 L231), 16 deg (cloverleaf L145, side_mount L142), 18 deg (001 L299, 005 L247, die_cast L255), 20 deg (004 L221).

parameters.name: mount_wall_m
parameters.rationale: Stamped plate thickness, or the wall of a sealed shell. Pool: 0.0017 (002 L73 extrude both=True), 0.002 (001 L28 box 2.0 mm), 0.003 (004 L57 extrude 1.5 both=True), 0.003 (side_mount L56 box y-thickness).

parameters.name: worm_span_m
parameters.rationale: Distance between the two worm bearing seats, i.e. the supported length of the vertical shaft. Pool: 0.024 (001 L183 bearings at z 7 and 31 mm), 0.032 (open_back_ratio L193/L199 at 7 and 39 mm), 0.034 (002 L112-L115 ears at 6 and 40 mm), 0.0215 (die_cast L34/L44 bosses at 1 and 31.5 mm).

parameters.name: worm_pitch_r_m
parameters.rationale: Worm pitch radius, read straight off `Worm.r0` in sdk/v0/gears.py so the template and the generator agree on where the pitch line is.

parameters.name: worm_tip_r_m
parameters.rationale: Worm tip radius (`Worm.ra`). Sizes the worm boss bore and the cavity a sealed shell has to hollow out around the thread.

parameters.name: center_distance_m
parameters.rationale: The common perpendicular between the two skew axes, laid along -X. Tangent pitch circles are the definition of a correct worm/wheel mesh; every station in the assembly is measured from it.

parameters.name: worm_len_m
parameters.rationale: Threaded length of the worm, in modules rather than in wheel radii: the pool runs 15-22 modules (001 18/1.0, 002 27/1.2, 003 12/0.8, 004 16/1.0, 005 14.5/0.66), and it still has to fit between the two bearing seats. Tying it to the wheel instead made the worm grow with the tooth count, which is both untrue to the sources and unaffordable -- each extra turn costs ~2.5k triangles on a spline-surfaced solid that collision QC re-evaluates at every pose.

parameters.name: worm_boss_r_m
parameters.rationale: Outer radius of the mount's worm bearing boss or ear ring; grows with the worm so a fat low-lead worm never bursts its bearing.

parameters.name: gear_chamber_r_m
parameters.rationale: Radius of the clear space the mount must leave around the driven wheel. The sealed candidates boolean-cut exactly this cavity, which is what lets a 30-tooth wheel live inside the same shell as a 14-tooth one instead of the combination being excluded.

parameters.name: mount_body_r_m
parameters.rationale: Outer radius of the mount around the wheel station -- the gear lobe of an open plate, the bulb of a gearbox pod, the half-height of a die-cast block.

parameters.name: worm_span_eff_m
parameters.rationale: Effective distance between the two worm bearings. The bearings have to STRADDLE the gear housing, so the declared span can never be shorter than the housing's own diameter -- 001 puts its bearings 24 mm apart around a 12 mm gear lobe. This is the derivation that keeps the button above every mount silhouette no matter which wheel the active post candidate brought with it.

parameters.name: mount_top_z_m
parameters.rationale: Top of the mount at the worm station: the upper bearing seat plus its own thickness. The button seat is measured from here, never from a constant.

parameters.name: mount_x0_m
parameters.rationale: Left edge of the mount: far enough past the worm boss of unit 0 to carry it.

parameters.name: mount_x1_m
parameters.rationale: Right edge: past the wheel lobe of the last unit. Together with mount_x0_m this is how the strip grows with N rather than being a fixed plate.

parameters.name: post_bore_r_m
parameters.rationale: Radius of the mount's post journal. The 0.4 mm running clearance stays inside the 1 mm gap the baseline QC still counts as support, so the post is carried without the bore having to interpenetrate it.

parameters.name: worm_bore_r_m
parameters.rationale: Radius of the mount's worm bearing bore, on the same clearance rule.

parameters.name: unit_pitch_m
parameters.rationale: Spacing of tuner units along +X. Every one of the three terms is a real interference: neighbouring wheels, neighbouring buttons at any rotation, and a worm boss reaching back into the previous wheel lobe. The button term normally dominates, which is why the strip widens when a big cloverleaf is fitted.

parameters.name: post_exit_y_m
parameters.rationale: The +Y face the string post emerges from; the free length of the post is measured from here so post_reach_m always means the visible projection.
